subject: Elevated 5xx/429s — request for SLA credit and incident escalation
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — urgent

Vanessa,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood endpoint for our /generate route around 07:20 PDT this morning. The errors persisted in waves and caused a number of our front-end clients to timeout and aggressively retry, which magnified load. Our observations: 
- ~20 minutes of elevated 5xx/429 starting ~07:20 — peak error rate ~18%.
- Numerous client-side retry storms (we have exponential backoff, but many short-lived sessions retried simultaneously).
- Throughput dropped ~60% during the spike and tail latency spiked beyond our SLA (p95 > 2.5s).

This impacted a significant portion of our users and could materially affect our renewal decision. We need:
1) Confirmation of what went wrong and exact incident window
2) A proposed SLA credit amount and timeline to apply it
3) Commitment on remediation and any configuration changes to prevent recurrence

Please escalate to engineering and legal as needed — Sasha and I are available for a call.

Thanks,
John
VP Product, Acme Corporation

[Attachment: sample-client-logs.txt]

Subject: RE: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — urgent

Vanessa, John — technical interim: 

Summary (initial triage):
- Incident window: 2026-03-15T07:18:00–2026-03-15T07:44:30 PDT (approx).
- Observed metrics: 5xx rate peaked at 18.3% (all backends), 429s peaked at 12.7%. Request throughput per shard fell ~58% at peak.
- Root cause (preliminary): a partial autoscaler misconfiguration combined with simultaneous client retries. One of the autoscaler controllers failed to scale additional worker groups due to a transient quota error when provisioning burst capacity in the us-west-2 region; as workers lagged, queue length grew, causing timeouts. Client retries then amplified the queue and produced additional 429 responses.
- Mitigation applied: manually provisioned burst workers and applied a temporary queuing throttle; by 07:44 PDT error rates returned to baseline.

Artifacts attached: incident-timeline-20260315.csv, error-aggregates-20260315.csv (attached).

Proposed immediate mitigations to prevent recurrence:
1) Harden autoscaler retry logic to tolerate quota transient errors (engineering change — ETA: 2 weeks for patch, 72h for emergency hotfix if approved).
2) Region-level capacity pre-warm policy for known large customers (product + sales discussion).
3) Implement server-side retry-suppression token to reduce retry storms from client libs (engineering + SDK owners).

For SLA credit calculation: we will provide official error-minute counts for your window and a suggested credit equal to pro-rated monthly fee for the impacted minutes, plus an additional 10% goodwill credit. I'll hand this to Vanessa for customer-facing numbers once we reconcile counts.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: error-aggregates-20260315.csv]

Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed credit and next steps (Acme outage 3/15)

John/Sasha — thanks for the patience. Attached are our reconciled counts and a proposed credit. Summary: 
- Confirmed incident window: 07:18–07:44:30 PDT on 2026-03-15.
- Impacted user requests (per your tenant): 1,842,300 requests attempted in-window; ~312k of those received 5xx/429s.
- Proposed goodwill + SLA credit: a pro-rated credit equal to 48 hours of service usage at your current committed rate, plus a one-time 10% goodwill bonus on top of that amount. We estimate the total credit to be $18,400 (draft).

We want to make this right and also lock in steps to prevent recurrence:
- Immediate (today): technical hotfix to autoscaler retry path to avoid failing the entire controller on quota errors (Marcus to prioritize).
- Next 72 hours: pre-warm capacity for scheduled Acme spikes (if you share traffic windows).
- 2 weeks: rollout hardened autoscaler and SDK token to dampen retry storms.

Please review the attached draft credit agreement (acme-credit-agreement-draft.pdf). If acceptable, Laura can formalize and route for signature. If you prefer a numeric change to the credit, let me know and I'll adjust. We're happy to hop on a call this afternoon to finalize.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: acme-credit-agreement-draft.pdf]
